title: Measures to Reduce and Compensate for Attrition of Doctors in Public Sector
what_it_is: Measures to Reduce and Compensate for Attrition of Doctors in Public Sector

sections.label: Doctor supply and attrition
sections.summary: Singapore admitted 40 more medical students yearly in 2020 and 2021, with about 200 overseas locals returning annually and doctor attrition of 3% to 5% from 2019 to 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In 2020 and 2021, we admitted another 40 medical students each year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: While our main source of doctors will continue to be our local medical schools, about 200 locals who study or practise medicine overseas return to Singapore annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Most of them study or work in Australia, the United Kingdom or Ireland.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Currently, the top five countries that our foreign doctors are recruited from are India, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines and the United Kingdom.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The attrition rate of doctors from the public healthcare sector into private practice is acceptable and it ranges from 3% to 5% in the time period 2019 to 2021.

sections.label: Medical student standards unchanged
sections.summary: The passage states that standards for medical students should not be altered in some way.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: On the first point of whether those standards for medical students should be altered in some way, I think he would agree with me that it should not.

sections.label: Safety standards for medical graduates
sections.summary: Medical graduates must meet the same safety requirements as other local university graduates before full registration, and these standards should not be reduced.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: In order to serve the mission to the public, we should hold them to the same safety requirements as any other graduate from a local university going out into medical practice.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And so, there is a standard set of approaches in order to make sure that they are safe to practise before they get fully registered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And I am sure the Member would agree – we should not reduce those standards.
